def min_weighted_completion(t, w, parent):
    """
    A build server runs n jobs one at a time, back to back, starting at
    time 0 (no idling between jobs).  Job i takes t[i] minutes and has
    urgency w[i].  parent[i] is the index of the single job that must
    finish before job i may start, or -1 if job i has no prerequisite.
    The prerequisite links form a forest: parent[i] is -1 or an index
    strictly less than i.

    A schedule is a permutation of all n jobs in which every job appears
    after its parent.  If job i finishes at time C_i, the schedule costs
    sum over i of w[i] * C_i.  Return the minimum possible cost over all
    valid schedules, as a single int.

    Input bounds: 1 <= n <= 200, with len(t) == len(w) == len(parent) == n,
    1 <= t[i] <= 10**4, and 0 <= w[i] <= 10**4.  (The number of valid
    schedules is factorial in n, so enumeration is hopeless at n = 200.)

    >>> min_weighted_completion([5], [7], [-1])
    35
    >>> min_weighted_completion([3, 1], [1, 10], [-1, -1])
    14
    >>> min_weighted_completion([3, 1, 1], [1, 100, 2], [-1, 0, -1])
    413
    """
